title: Path traversal: files outside the folder
summary: A file name from a request reaches the file system. See how ../ and Path.Combine's rooted-path rule escape the folder, then resolve and confine every path the safe way.

steps.title: The request and what the server opens
body: Two things go wrong. `..` climbs out of the folder. And `Path.Combine` has a rule that surprises most people: **if a later part is rooted, the earlier parts are dropped**. `Path.Combine("/work/data/invoices", "/etc/passwd")` is `/etc/passwd`. On Windows, `C:\Windows\win.ini` and `\\server\share` are rooted too.

What an attacker reads depends on the process's rights: config files with connection strings, `/proc/self/environ` (the process's environment variables, often full of secrets), source code, other customers' files. Running as a low-privilege user limits the damage, which is why containers should not run as root.

steps.prompt: What does `Path.Combine` give for each input? (This runs on Linux paths with forward slashes; read it as the shop would.)
steps.explain: A rooted second argument replaces the first in `Path.Combine`. A relative one with `..` is appended, and `..` is only resolved later, when the path is opened or passed to `Path.GetFullPath`.

steps.title: Resolve, then confine
body: Do not try to clean the input (`file.Replace("../", "")` turns `....//` into `../`). Instead let the framework **resolve** the path, then check where it ended up:
var full = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(root, file));      // resolves .. and rooted paths
The **separator at the end of `root` matters**: `/work/data/invoices-old/ledger.txt` starts with `/work/data/invoices`, but not with `/work/data/invoices/`.
Even better options, when you can:
- **Do not take paths at all**: take an order id, check ownership, and build the file name yourself (`invoice-{order.Id}.pdf`).
- `new PhysicalFileProvider(root).GetFileInfo(name)` refuses absolute paths and paths that leave the root.

steps.prompt: `root` is `/work/data/invoices/`. After `Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(root, file))`, does the result pass the `StartsWith(root)` check?
steps.explain: `..` that stays inside is harmless after resolving. Anything that ends up outside is refused, however it was spelled.

steps.prompt: A reviewer suggests: `if (file.Contains("..")) return BadRequest();`. What is wrong with that as the only check?
options: It misses rooted paths such as /etc/passwd, which need no .. at all
Nothing: without .. there is no traversal
It blocks every file name with a dot
steps.explain: `Path.Combine(root, "/etc/passwd")` escapes without a single dot. String checks on the input chase spellings; checking the resolved path covers every spelling at once.

steps.title: SafeInvoicePath
prompt: Write `string? SafeInvoicePath(string root, string file)`. It returns the **full path** of `file` inside the folder `root`, or `null` when the resolved path is not strictly inside `root` (the folder itself does not count).
The tests use a temporary folder, so they work on Windows and Linux alike.
solution: // Strictly inside: the folder itself ("root/" or "root/.") is not a file.
return full.Length > rootFull.Length && full.StartsWith(rootFull, StringComparison.Ordinal) ? full : null;
hints: Make the root end with a separator first: `var rootFull = Path.GetFullPath(root) + Path.DirectorySeparatorChar;` (skip the extra one if it already ends with one).
`var full = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(rootFull, file)); return full.StartsWith(rootFull, StringComparison.Ordinal) ? full : null;`
template: Dojo.Eq("a plain invoice name", Path.Combine(dojoRoot, "invoice-1001.txt"), SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot, "invoice-1001.txt"));
Dojo.Eq("a sub-folder is fine", Path.Combine(dojoRoot, "2026", "invoice-7.txt"), SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot, $"2026{sep}invoice-7.txt"));
Dojo.Eq("a .. that stays inside is fine", Path.Combine(dojoRoot, "invoice-7.txt"), SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot, $"2026{sep}..{sep}invoice-7.txt"));
Dojo.Eq("../ out of the folder is refused", null, SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot, $"..{sep}..{sep}secret.txt"));
Dojo.Eq("a sibling folder with the same prefix is refused", null, SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot, $"..{sep}invoices-old{sep}ledger.txt"));
Dojo.Eq("an absolute path is refused", null, SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot, Path.Combine(dojoBase, "config.json")));
Dojo.Eq("the folder itself is refused", null, SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot, "."));
Dojo.Eq("an empty name is refused", null, SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot, ""));
Dojo.Eq("a root given with a trailing separator works too", Path.Combine(dojoRoot, "a.txt"), SafeInvoicePath(dojoRoot + sep, "a.txt"));

steps.title: Live lab: read /etc/passwd, then confine the path
prompt: In the **vulnerable shop** lab, do **Attack: read /etc/passwd** (the invoice download takes any file name) and **Fix: resolve the path and confine it** in `Invoices.cs`. The check includes the `invoices-old` sibling folder: make sure your prefix ends with a separator.
steps.explain: Resolving then checking the prefix (with the separator) blocks every spelling the check tries: `../`, absolute paths, encoded slashes and the sibling folder.
